report:
The proposed construction answers ORIGINAL P15.1 as literally stated. Its essential proofs and external theorem applications check out. This verdict does not rely on the earlier partial labels, scoped reviews, source hashes, compilation, or arithmetic diagnostics.

The governing wording is: “choose the minimum necessary reference scale and construct a path-independent unnormalized energy theory”; the perturbation obligation is to “prove independence of the stated perturbation choices.” Section 9.2 additionally requires: “Name the reference scale, dimensional carrier and retained singularity data.” These requirements do not prescribe equality of actual-current degree with numerical dimension, a geometric d-dimensional quotient, or agreement with every simultaneous unbounded perturbation limit. The description of an earlier attempted class-volume construction does not make that particular method mandatory. P15.2 and P15.3 remain separate targets.

The external foundations were checked against the opened primary sources: [BEGZ](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0812.3674v2), [DDNL](https://msp.org/apde/2018/11-8/apde-v11-n8-p06-s.pdf), [Vu’s energy paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2005.13241v3), [Vu’s relative-product paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2004.11111v1), [DGMS](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~dennis/publications/PDF/DS-pub-0024.pdf), and [Guedj–Zeriahi](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~guedj/fichierspdf/JGA05.pdf). DDNL’s mixed-mass theorems explicitly permit pseudoeffective backgrounds. Vu’s diagonal convexity theorem applies to an arbitrary positive reference P; no minimal-singularity or model-reference hypothesis is missing. The local convergence and locality applications respect their bounded-product-factor hypotheses.

The actual degree is established correctly. Positive comparison of Kähler forms makes positivity of each trace mass independent of the auxiliary form. Multilinearity gives the actual perturbed mass polynomial. Its mass is bounded by the minimal-singularity mass in the big perturbed class, whose volume tends to zero. Consequently M_n=0 and d<n. Filling unused slots with smooth Kähler factors makes every DDNL application legitimate. More-singular mixed products of degree greater than d have zero positive trace mass and therefore vanish as currents. Closedness and smooth Stokes establish the asserted auxiliary-class mass polynomials. Nothing identifies these actual masses with class positive products.

The bounded integration-by-parts reconstruction uses the correct identity da∧dᶜa R = ½ddᶜ(a²)R − a ddᶜa R. Its local square coefficients 1, 1, −½ follow by expanding (A−B)². The cutoff estimate ∫dζ_k∧dᶜζ_k R ≤ 4k⁻¹∫ΩR and the uniform truncated-difference gradient bound make the boundary terms tend to zero by Cauchy–Schwarz. Locality is used on the cutoff’s nonzero locus, not its closed support. The signed products and intrinsic gradients have the requisite finite mass and admissibility. Vu’s operator is twice the submitted operator, so source potentials are halved and multiplying the source identity by two gives the submitted normalization. Thus the printed half-factor defects are not inherited. The unused defective v1 arguments are unnecessary.

On each bounded finite convex hull, the coefficient integrals are finite polynomials. Signed differentiation and the checked bounded IBP make the polynomial one-form closed. Stokes on triangles proves the cocycle, and the beta integral gives exactly the factor 1/(q+1). The first and second segment derivatives prove monotonicity and concavity; same-type mixed mass gives the constant-shift and supremum-norm bounds. Auxiliary representative changes transfer ddᶜ to the bounded potential difference. The resulting degree-(d+1) products vanish, proving representative independence in every complementary slot, including d=0. Decomposition into differences of Kähler forms then yields the claimed symmetric class functional. Smooth θ-gauge changes preserve the currents and differences exactly.

The common-domain argument is valid without assuming positivity of a difference current. Each scalar deficit against ω₁ʲ(Aω₀−ω₁)^(m−j) is nonnegative by DDNL, and their positively weighted sum is zero. Hence every deficit vanishes. Polynomial extraction gives equality against mixed complementary Kähler factors. Pointwise comparison of positive complementary forms proves that joint weighted finiteness is independent of every fixed auxiliary class and representative. For d≥1, the source joint linear energy is precisely d/2 times the binomially weighted submitted integrals after normalization, so Vu’s convexity theorem applies to exactly this domain. For d=0, full mass is automatic and smooth-volume L¹ integrability supplies the argument directly.

Convexity also supplies every required mixed mass and weighted integral. Expanding the average of a finite family gives mixed masses bounded above by M_d whose average equals M_d; each therefore equals M_d. Weighted convexity and 0≤ψ−u_i≤N(ψ−w) give integrability against every mixed degree-d product. These facts establish the hypotheses needed subsequently; they are not merely conditional implications.

The truncation identity is exact. Original and truncated products agree on {u>ψ−L}, after bounded local truncation and exhaustion of the finite loci. Their total masses agree, so their complementary masses agree. The boundary weight is exactly L, giving ∫(ψ−u_L)dμ_{a,L}=∫min(ψ−u,L)dμ_a. Monotone convergence proves both the finite integral formula and its equivalence with a finite truncation-energy limit. Constants handle u≤ψ+C. Bounded decreasing continuity follows from bounded local weighted convergence and the equal-total-mass tail estimate. General decreasing capacity convergence is correctly deduced from bounded GZ convergence plus the sublevel estimate. Sandwiching by relative truncations then proves decreasing continuity on F¹ and transfers concavity.

The unbounded cocycle has the necessary tail control: on the complementary simultaneous truncation set, Lν_{a,L}(B_L)=Lν_a(B_L)≤∫_{B_L}((ψ−u)+(ψ−v))dν_a→0. The original difference has an integrable tail as well. Thus the bounded cocycle passes to the displayed finite mixed-integral formula. This establishes endpoint-independent energy increments throughout F¹ without invoking unbounded-velocity differential calculus. Bounded-equivalent anchors have identical domains and the exact origin-change cocycle. Representative independence follows by taking the already established bounded truncation limits.

The coefficient extension and minimum-reference theorem are also complete. Kähler pure powers span Sym^m V because an annihilating homogeneous polynomial would vanish on an open cone and hence vanish identically. Finitely many such powers therefore give an invertible evaluation map. Convergence of the finite truncation energies at those classes forces coefficientwise convergence. Mixed complementary truncation identities and finite signed decompositions verify the explicit unbounded integral formula. Finite-dimensional closedness then proves that the unbounded functional span equals the bounded span S, rather than merely being contained in an unspecified larger space.

It follows that equality of all anchored F¹ energies is equivalent to equality of q(λ^m). Constants place the positive raw-mass functional in S, so this quotient retains scale. The linear factorization statement concerns the full tensor family on B: any descriptor through which its linear functionals factor has kernel contained in K and consequently maps surjectively onto Q. For actual Kähler auxiliaries, the separate set-descriptor theorem gives the coarsest information I. These are the necessary/sufficient minimum data for the constructed theory, which is what the literal request for an energy theory requires. The dossier does not formulate a stronger minimum across every conceivable energy theory. This distinction is explicit, rather than a substitution of an unproved geometric minimum. The finite-coordinate argument also proves the claimed quotient topology and simultaneous decreasing-potential/quotient continuity.

The perturbation prescription satisfies its stated independence requirements. The exact expansion has coefficients binom(n,k)ε^(n−k)E^k; the subset identity and segment integration give the asserted coefficients. Bounded differences control each lower coefficient by ||u−ψ||∞M_k. Convergent auxiliary classes keep the mass polynomials bounded, so division by binom(n,d)ε^m suppresses every lower term and leaves the degree-d energy. Uniformly approaching same-type perturbed potentials have error at most their supremum error times the actual perturbed anchor mass, yielding the same limit. No uniform representative bounds are required for this bounded assertion.

For F¹, the submission explicitly chooses the bounded leading limit first and the truncation limit second. Both limits are already proved, and their result is the finite mixed-integral construction. Its independence of truncation levels, bounded decreasing approximations, representatives, coordinate bases, and equivalent anchors follows from the established identities. This is a completed prescription, not a future proposal. The concentration example correctly shows why a stronger unrestricted joint limit cannot be added: its top-energy quotient is E_{0,λ}(u)+ε∫vκ_ε, with the second term tending to minus infinity although all auxiliary classes coincide. That counterexample does not contradict any perturbation limit asserted by the new submission or impose an unstated obligation on P15.1.

The examples check analytically. The radial potential has positive inner Hessian, no point atom, total mass one, and finite singular weighted integral because ∫s^(2a−2)ds converges for a<1/2. It genuinely extends the bounded domain. The product-surface quotient computation follows from fiberwise constancy and the wedge calculation. The divisor reference has d=0 while the smooth reference in the same nef class has d=1; its actual perturbed mass and the class volume have the different stated leading exponents. This confirms why the construction must retain actual singularity data and must not substitute a class-volume coefficient.

Every pseudoeffective zero-volume class admits a reference, and each resulting F¹ contains its bounded comparison domain. Defining this natural finite-energy domain does not exclude ambient classes. The named carrier is X, of complex dimension n, with current product degree d; the literal carrier requirement is met. If disconnected manifolds are admitted, the compact manifold has finitely many components. Selecting nontrivial references componentwise, retaining their possibly different degrees and scales, and summing their energies preserves the cocycles. Independent componentwise inputs establish the corresponding product minimum-reference criterion. No cross-component equality of degrees or scales is required.

Three harmless wording clarifications should accompany acceptance. First, the leading actual mass coefficient is binom(n,d)M_d, and its leading term is binom(n,d)M_dε^m; the displayed denominator binom(n,d)ε^m deliberately leaves raw mass intact. Second, “anchor independence” means invariance with the proved cocycle origin adjustment, not equality of numerical anchored values. Third, genuinely unbounded inputs are possible, as the example proves; they need not exist for every reference type, such as the trivial zero-class case. These clarifications change no formula or indispensable proof.

passages.statement: On a compact Kähler n-fold, the nonpluripolar product of k closed positive (1,1) currents, 1≤k≤n, is a finite closed positive current, symmetric, multilinear under sums of positive currents, and plurifinely local. Its trace measures do not charge pluripolar sets, and smooth positive factors act by ordinary wedge multiplication (BEGZ, Definition 1.1, Propositions 1.4 and 1.6, Theorem 1.8).

passages.statement: On a compact Kähler n-fold, the nonpluripolar product of k closed positive (1,1) currents, 1≤k≤n, is a finite closed positive current, symmetric, multilinear under sums of positive currents, and plurifinely local. Its trace measures do not charge pluripolar sets, and smooth positive factors act by ordinary wedge multiplication (BEGZ, Definition 1.1, Propositions 1.4 and 1.6, Theorem 1.8).

Let X be a compact Kähler n-fold, θ_j smooth closed real (1,1) forms with pseudoeffective classes, and u_j,v_j∈PSH(X,θ_j), for 1≤j≤n. Equal bounded singularity types in every slot imply equal integrals of the top mixed nonpluripolar products. If v_j≤u_j+C_j in every slot, the u-product integral is at least the v-product integral (DDNL, Proposition 2.1 and Theorem 2.4).

Let X be a compact Kähler n-fold, θ_j smooth closed real (1,1) forms with pseudoeffective classes, and u_j,v_j∈PSH(X,θ_j), for 1≤j≤n. Equal bounded singularity types in every slot imply equal integrals of the top mixed nonpluripolar products. If v_j≤u_j+C_j in every slot, the u-product integral is at least the v-product integral (DDNL, Proposition 2.1 and Theorem 2.4).

On a compact Kähler manifold, positive currents in a pseudoeffective class have global potentials for any smooth representative, and minimal-singularity potentials exist. In a big class their top nonpluripolar mass equals its volume. For pseudoeffective α and every Kähler class λ, vol(α+ελ) tends to vol(α) as ε decreases to zero. Positive products of nef classes equal their cup products (BEGZ, §§1.3–1.4, Definition 1.17).

On a compact Kähler n-fold, for a closed positive current R of bidegree (n−1,n−1) and bounded R-admissible dsh functions a,b, intrinsic Dirichlet products are finite, their diagonal is positive, and ∫b⟨ddᶜa·∧R⟩=∫a⟨ddᶜb·∧R⟩=−∫⟨db∧dᶜa·∧R⟩. Admissibility means R does not charge the quasi-psh representation poles (Vu, Lemmas 2.5–2.6 and Theorem 2.7).
passages.quote: Let v, w be bounded T-admissible dsh functions on X.

passages.statement: Let X be compact Kähler, P=θ+ddᶜφ positive in a pseudoeffective class, 1≤k≤n, and R smooth closed positive of bidegree (n−k,n−k). Among θ-psh u≤φ+C, both the class satisfying {⟨T_u^k·∧R⟩}={⟨P^k·∧R⟩} and its subclass satisfying ∑_{a=0}^k∫|u−φ|⟨T_u^aP^(k−a)·∧R⟩<∞ are convex (Vu, Section 3 and Theorem 3.4 with χ(t)=t).

passages.statement: For a fixed Kähler form Ω on a compact Kähler manifold, negative nontrivial Ω-psh functions f satisfy Cap_Ω({f<−A})≤C_Ω(1+||f||_{L¹(Ω^n)})/A for A>0. Bounded Ω-psh functions decreasing to a bounded Ω-psh limit converge in capacity. Ω-psh functions are quasicontinuous, and global Kähler capacity is comparable to the summed local Bedford–Taylor capacities on a finite relatively compact chart cover (Guedj–Zeriahi, Propositions 3.6, 3.7 and 3.10, Corollary 3.8).

On an open subset of C^n, uniformly bounded local psh functions converging in capacity in all n slots, together with uniformly bounded quasicontinuous weights converging in capacity to a quasicontinuous weight, have weakly convergent weighted Bedford–Taylor top products (DDNL, Proposition 2.2).

On an open subset of C^n, uniformly bounded local psh functions converging in capacity in all n slots, together with uniformly bounded quasicontinuous weights converging in capacity to a quasicontinuous weight, have weakly convergent weighted Bedford–Taylor top products (DDNL, Proposition 2.2).

On U⊂C^n, let R be closed positive and let bounded psh product factors u_j,u'_j coincide on W=⋂_i{v_i>v'_i}, where v_i,v'_i are possibly unbounded psh functions. For product degrees compatible with R, their Bedford–Taylor products relative to R agree after restriction to W (Vu, Theorem 3.3).

On a compact Kähler manifold, a smooth differential form that is d-closed, dᶜ-closed and d-exact is ddᶜ-exact with a smooth primitive; this holds over the reals. In particular, cohomologous smooth real closed (1,1) forms differ by ddᶜg for a smooth real function g, with the operator’s scalar normalization adjusted (DGMS, Lemma 5.11 and Remark 5.14).

passages.statement: On a compact Kähler n-fold, relative nonpluripolar products of k closed positive (1,1) currents with a closed positive current R of bidegree (p,p), k+p≤n, are well-defined. Their iterated-product identity holds whenever the relevant products are defined, and they preserve absence of mass on complete pluripolar sets uncharged by R (Vu, Lemma 3.4 and Proposition 3.5(iii),(vi); also Proposition 2.1(iii) of the energy paper). Vu’s relative-product convention is ddᶜ=i∂∂̄/π.
